Butt-Monkey: At the hands of his own recruits no less in "The Movie." Depending on the Writer: His characterization switches between extremes. Comics present him as a relaxed, thoughtful man who avoids strife, while cartoons portray him as very irritable. The one constant is that he abhors laziness. And then there's his appearance in theSpy TroopsCGI movie fromThe Aughties, where he got a surfer personality complete with voice by Matt Hill.

characters.name: Grunt
characters.description: An infantryman who would later leave the Joes to get his engineering degree. Genius Bruiser: He's both an engineer as well as infantryman. Happily Married: To his wife, Lola. They met after he retired from the Joes. Origins Episode:GI Joe Declassifiedwas an issue showing how he ended up joining the military as opposed to a Cobra soldier. 10-Minute Retirement: Some of the Grunts in continuity come back after leaving.

characters.name: Flash
characters.description: Energy Weapon: His specialty as a laser rifle trooper; it helps him to identify that the orbital laser beams are low-power and harmless duringRevolution. Forced Transformation:Gets transmuted into a Dire Wraith by theTalisman. Pungeon Master: Apparently a tendency of his. Retcon: Was first seen as a picture in Duke's wallet alongside various dead Joes, but shows up alive and well duringRevolution.

characters.name: Wild Bill
characters.description: A former Long Range Recon Patrol officer who transferred to the Armored Air Cavalry Division, Wild Bill serves as the Joes' ground support chopper pilot. Ace Pilot: Of both, fixed (Airplanes) and rotary (Helicopters) wings. And he rides that consarned 'ssault gunship XH-1 Dragonfly of his as if it were a true bronco colt!Wild Weasel:Nobody can do that with a FANG!Nobody!Wild Bill:...wellmy nameain't"Nobody"!. Cavalry Officer: Know buckaroo the man's actually thatnoteArmoured Air Cavalry, that is!... and at times, dresses up like one. Catchphrase: "Well... Shoot fire!" Cowboy: Types II and III for sure.

characters.name: Doc I
characters.description: Ascended Extra: Ironically enough, all his major appearances wereafterhe passed-on his codename to his daughter. Formerly Fit: He puts on a lot of weight between volume 3 and volume 5. Heroic Sacrifice:When Skywarp's teleport test malfunctions and sends shrapnel everywhere, Doc takes the bullet for Grand Slam, revealing his true heritage.Skywarp, predictably, feels nothing over this. My Species Doth Protest Too Much:He's a Dire Wraith. Non-Action Guy: Operates out of the Joes' base, in contrast to his daughter, who acts as their field medic.

characters.name: Doc II
characters.description: Barrier Warrior: Uses a portable energy shield in combat. Deadpan Snarker: Makes a few jabs at her allies' less sensible decisions.Mostly Rock'n'Roll's. Half-Human Hybrid:Half Dire Wraith. Legacy Character: The second user of the "Doc" codename, after her father. Traumatic Superpower Awakening:The possibility of being dissected to see if she's half-Wraith causes her Wraith heritage to flare up.

characters.name: Hashtag
characters.description: Does Not Like Guns: Which the other team members are pretty incredulous about, given thatshe joined the Army. Idiot Ball: Seriously, how dense do you have to be toupdate social media with your locationin the middle of an infiltration mission?

characters.name: Big Ben
characters.description: I Am Very British: His name isn't subtle. Parental Neglect: As he's dying, he expresses regret that he wasn't a big enough part of his daughter's life. Remember the New Guy?: The first time we ever see him is as an ex-Joe working with Duke as a mercenary in Eastern Europe. Sacrificial Lion: Is killed off in the start of the Revolution crossover after warningAction Manabout the Ore-13 crystals.

characters.name: Grand Slam
characters.description: The Bus Came Back: After only appearing briefly in the Origins mini-series, he returns in Vol. 5 as part of the main cast. Career-Ending Injury:Being shot. Only Mostly Dead: Twice.The bullet that was fired into his brain was half an inch away from hitting a fatal area.He survives Rock'n'Roll shooting him, but in a wheelchair. The bullet that was fired into his brain was half an inch away from hitting a fatal area. He survives Rock'n'Roll shooting him, but in a wheelchair.

characters.name: Chuckles
characters.description: A former CID investigator who serves as the Joes' primary deep cover operative. His only animated participation was inG.I. Joe: The Moviebut he was more prominent in several comic continuities. Alliterative Name:PhilProvost The Big Guy: His introduction inThe Movieshows him not caring too much about the required calculation to fire a missile while learning how to operate a H.A.V.O.C. vehicle. He simply jumped out from the cockpit after it's left CIWS malfunctioned and carried the missile throwing it at one of the captured automated HISS tanks, instead. Boisterous Bruiser: His fighting style. Cowboy Cop: Had this reputation in the CID before he joined the Joes.

characters.name: Jinx
characters.description: Adaptational Jerkass: Jinx is usually a kindheartedCute Clumsy Girlwho fights alongside her fellow Joes, but on here she initially begins as a confrontational, arrogant warrior taunting the Joes for being weaker and has a blatant dislike of Scarlett. Not to mention, she briefly becomes a merciless merc helping Destro's coup. She gets better over time. Age Lift: Most interpretations of her are grown adult women, but this incarnation of Jinx is young enough to be mistaken for a teenager. Arrogant Kung-Fu Guy: She's not at all shy about her martial arts skills. During training she taunts the Joes for barely keeping up with her and is instantly envious ofScarlett. Born Unlucky: She earned her nickname Jinx because she has theworstluck. Best shown when she tries to escape her cousin all by herself only to accidentally injure herselfandland in a pit of venomous snakes, needing rescuing again. Broken Pedestal: Snake Eyes becomes one for her when she discovers he had a hand in her father's death. Storm Shadow sways her over to his darkside and trains her to be a villainous mercenary for hire. However...Rebuilt Pedestal: Once Snake Eyes and Scarlett confront her again, they reveal the truth. Snake Eyes tried saving her father only to be framed. Leading to her regaining respect for Snake once more and undergoing aHeel–Face Turn.

characters.name: Flint
characters.description: Voice Actor: Johnny Messner Adaptational Jerkass: Flint is most famous for being the classic manly action hero archetype, tough when he's in a fight, but has a kind heart and friendly nature all around. This incarnation is a bit more gruff, harsh, and confrontational whenever onscreen. The Atoner: Seems to carry a lot of guilt over sacking Duke back in their school football days, as Duke was seriously injured and missed out on scholarship money his family needed. Flint has tried to make it up to him several times since, and even while chasing the Joes, he's convinced himself he's doing Duke a favor. Butt-Monkey: His efforts in turning in the Joes often don't turn out well. By-the-Book Cop: As a contrast to Duke, who's willing to forgo the law or authority if doing so proves the right thing to do in his heart, Flint is by the book. As mentioned above, the truth (and by extension, what's wrong or right) are for the due processes of the law to ascertain.

characters.name: Chameleon
characters.description: Adaptational Badass: Astoria in the cartoon was mostly helpless. This Astoria is a trained sniper and martial artist, who also isn't afraid to make use of advanced tech to her advantage in a fight. Adaptational Intelligence: The original Astoria was a sweet girl, but not too bright, and was the figurehead of her family company. Here, she's the true power behind Hybrid Technologies, and is onlyObfuscating Stupidity. Adaptational Villainy: In the past, Chameleon was a Joe who used her striking physical similarity to the Baroness to infiltrate Cobra. Here, she's willingly working for Cobra. Likewise, herSecret Identity, Astoria Carlton-Ritz, was an ally of the Autobots inThe Transformers. Ambiguously Human: Issue #24 shows her experiencing a nightmare where half of her face is mechanical, implying her cybernetic implants weren'tjustregulated to her arm. Composite Character: Of the original Astoria Carlton-Ritz fromThe Transformers, and of Chameleon from G.I. Joe, who was originally aToyline-Exclusive Character. She also takes the original role of the Baroness as Destro’s lover and confidante.

characters.name: Ronin
characters.description: All Asians Know Martial Arts Impaled with Extreme Prejudice:Stabbed through the chest by Storm Shadow while protecting Billy. 10-Minute Retirement: Quits the team after trying and failing to rescue Chuckles (who didn't want to be rescued), but later returns to the fold.

characters.name: Lady Jaye
characters.description: Voice Actor:Nika Futterman Action Girl: As always, she's a very active female character. Her role in the series means she doesn't get to show this often, but she's never shy to do so whenever the chance presents itself. Beauty Equals Goodness: As opposed toThe Baroness, Jaye is a very beautiful woman who also does the right thing. Her main role being assisting the Joes in their escapes from time to time because she truly believes they're innocent people falsely accused. Cute Bruiser: As per norm, Lady Jaye looks more like an adorable model rather than a professional seasoned marine. Deadpan Snarker: From time to time she can drop a good jab at her foolish cohorts, especially towards Flint or the Baroness.Flint:Freeze!(Sees Snake Eyes left his tracking device on a squirrel.)Lady Jaye:You wanna cuff him or should I?

characters.name: Clockspring
characters.description: Dude, Where's My Respect?:Tomax manipulates him by preying on the fact that the others don't appreciate how rare his skills are. Entitled to Have You: Resents Chameleon for not returning his affections or paying much attention to him, and Flint for hooking up with her instead. Jerkass: Quickly becomes one. Redemption Equals Death:Sacrifices himself by ensuring that the civilians and other Joes can be evacuated from the casino, before detonating the explosions while the Cobra operatives are still inside. Unwitting Pawn:Gets manipulated by Tomax into helping him take back control of the casino in which the intelligence unit is based.

characters.name: Firewall
characters.description: Reluctant Retiree: Was transferred from the front lines to a desk job after an injury, and never allowed to return. Younger than She Looks: Her hair went grey early from stress.

characters.name: Skywarp
characters.description: The Brute: Big, intimidating, and brutal. No Sympathy: Considering he views organics as vermin, it's no surprise that he barely reacts toDoc'sHeroic Sacrifice. Teleportation: Not anymore; thanks to his repairs at the hands of the EDC, his teleportation abilities have been removed, and he's hanging around the Joes until they can be restored. Token Evil Teammate: He's been described by the author as "the team'sVegeta".

characters.name: Mayday
characters.description: Ascended Extra: She was originally just a background character inTransformers: Robots in Disguise, who John Barber took a liking to after giving her a few lines. Black Boss Lady: Was the second in command of the EDC, and serves as a Warrant Officer for the Joes. BFG: Carries one inRevolutionaries. Deadpan Snarker: Does a lot of commenting with wry amusement on the Transformers' antics. My Greatest Failure:Flash, Heavy Duty and Quarrel were mutated into Dire Wraiths on her watch.

characters.name: Quarrel
characters.description: Canon Immigrant: FromAction Force, the British version of G.I. Joe. Forced Transformation:Gets transmuted into a Dire Wraith by theTalisman.

characters.name: Talon
characters.description: Artistic License – Military: Zilong is listed as a "Pilot (First Class)"... but assuming the same ranking structure as the PLA Air Force, that would make him just a junior enlisted airman. Freudian Excuse: Hates Cybertronians because he was there on the day that they destroyed Beijing. Hair-Trigger Temper: Seems to have developed one inOptimus Prime. Irony:Though it's not been commented on, both Seekers who destroyed Beijing, Thundercracker and Skywarp, now work with G.I. Joe in some capacity. The latter is even a field operative.When the Junkions arrive, he fires on the Autobots to try and force them back onto their ship and let the humans handle first contact. The Junkions like the Autobots better and find him annoying so they leave the area as well. Though it's not been commented on, both Seekers who destroyed Beijing, Thundercracker and Skywarp, now work with G.I. Joe in some capacity. The latter is even a field operative.

characters.name: Spike
characters.description: Adaptation Personality Change: From aWide-Eyed IdealistKid-Appeal Characterand friend to the Autobots to aJerkass, self-centered military brat who works against them. Elites Are More Glamorous: His military specialty is listed as "special warfare operations". The Friend Nobody Likes: Everyone he works with sees him as an unlikeable, self-centeredJerkasswhothinks he's the hero of an action movie. Even Zilong Qian, who he considers a friend, is implied to hate him. Hate Sink:Nobodylikes him. Smug Snake: He's one arrogant bastard.

characters.name: Hi-Tech
characters.description: The Bus Came Back: He was originally in theBumblebeeminiseries tie-in all the way back inThe Transformers (IDW). After that story concluded he disappeared from the narrative, only to reappear in Bumblebee's spotlight tie-in toThe Transformers: Dark Cybertronand later appear as a semi-regular in RID's Earth Arc. Legacy Character: The original Hi-Tech was possessed by a Dire Wraith and killed duringRevolution. Nice Guy: Laid back and accommodating to his staff and coworkers. Buster seems fond of him. Only Sane Man: During season 2 ofThe Transformers: Robots in Disguise. Transplant: He was created as a non-Joe-related character forThe Transformers (IDW), and folded into G.I. Joe.

characters.name: Salvo
characters.description: A rough and tumble Joe with a distrust of high-tech weapons. Boring, but Practical: His original file-card says Salvo distrusts complex weapons due to their potential unreliability, instead carrying a large amount of conventional weapon "to overwhelm enemy forces with massive expenditures of sheer firepower". Brainwashed and Crazy: The first regular episode of theDiCcartoon had him inhale a mind control gas and become a mindless minion of Cobra Commander. Gender LiftandRace Lift: InG.I. Joe (2016), Salvo is a Samoan woman. Might Makes Right: His motto is "THE RIGHT OF MIGHT", scrawled on his t-shirt.

characters.name: MP3
characters.description: Black Dude Dies First: Averted, Misfire and Krok merely think him dead. Canon Foreigner: Created forThe Transformers: More than Meets the Eyeas a tie intoRevolution. Hero of Another Story: While his teammates deal with the Dire Wraiths in Monument Valley, he's seeing a robot dinosaur rampage through a town. Locked Out of the Loop: Has no idea what MASK is. Mythology Gag: his group name and vehicle are references to the British localizations of G.I Joe, Action Force and Action Man.

characters.name: G.I. Joe
characters.description: Adaptational Villainy:If it means testing an anti-Cybertronian weapon, he has no problems with hiring super-villains. Ascended Fanboy: He was inspired by Sergeant Savage and his Screaming Eagles. Big Good: Through volume 3, he's the authority figure the Joes answer to. Broken Pedestal:Scarlett used to look up to him, but is disillusioned after learning that he is Baron Ironblood and intent on committing genocide against the Cybertronians. Composite Character:To faciliate his goal to wipe out the Cybertronians, he takes on the identity of Baron Ironblood, a character who originated as the arch enemy of G.I. Joe's UK equivalent Action Force.

characters.name: Miles Mayhem
characters.description: Big Bad Wannabe: OfRevolution. Composite Character: Between Miles Mayhem ofM.A.S.K.and the G.I. Joe Sea Adventurer. Destructive Savior: Even while he was nominally a good guy he didn't give a damn about collateral damage. Why do you think he's called Mayhem? Fantastic Racism: Doesn't like Cybertronians, at all. It's All About Me: It has to behimwho makes theHeroic Sacrificethat saves Earth and is viewed as a hero. Not Optimus Prime.

characters.name: Bulletman
characters.description: Humble Beginnings: Hails from the small town ofPoverty Flat. Glory Seeker: He's always been after fame. The Mentor: To Cover Girl. Retired Badass: He's not a hero anymore, but he can still kick ass. Self-Made Man: Created the helmet and jetpack that effectively gave him superpowers himself.

characters.name: Atomic Man
characters.description: Came Back Wrong:After his death, he revives in the body of the Maximal Centurion, with their not quite being aMental Fusion. Disability Superpower: Born with a missing arm and leg, which enabled him to build his atomic-powered prosthetics. Kid Detective: Was one of these in his youth. Self-Made Man: Built his atomic limbs himself (albeit with the help of an alien artifact).

characters.name: Baroness
characters.description: Voice Actor: Tatyana Yassukovich Adaptational Badass:Much more effective in combat than her main series counterpart.The fact that the Oktober Guard, an entire resistance group, who in mainline canon was the Soviet answer to GI Joe, has apparently been fighting against her family specifically for literal generations highlights just how powerful and dangerous her family is. Much more effective in combat than her main series counterpart. The fact that the Oktober Guard, an entire resistance group, who in mainline canon was the Soviet answer to GI Joe, has apparently been fighting against her family specifically for literal generations highlights just how powerful and dangerous her family is. Adaptational Modesty: Her femme fatale traits are altered in order to make her aLady of Warinstead. Anastasia lacks her iconicSpy Catsuitleather and is often seen in aBadass Longcoatcovering everything instead. Though, she shares her other counterparts taste for gorgeous dresses when playing up her businesswoman persona.

characters.name: Destro
characters.description: Voice Actor:Clancy Brown Adaptational Origin Connection: Normally he's already wearing his mask when he joins Cobra; the origin varies. Here, he's forced to don the maskas Cobra Commander's punishment for Destro's attempted betrayal. Adaptational Wimp: This Destro is not even half as clever as the Commander is. In most Joe media, Destro's usually on equal footing with his partner in crime or even a full-onDragon-in-Chiefwhose the real power behind COBRA. However, this version is outsmarted and beaten in his place by the head snake. Even Dr. Mindbender is not afraid to mock him to his face. Amazon Chaser: Lets out a lovesick sigh watching Baroness kick ass. And I Must Scream: Here, his mask is implied to bescrewed into his skull.

characters.name: Krake
characters.description: Contrasting Sequel Antagonist: Compared to the original Cobra Commander, he'sfarmore militaristic and aggressive. From Nobody to Nightmare: Started out born to an impoverished family on a battlefield in Nanzhao, and worked his way up to the top through sheer brutality. No Name Given: Because, apparently, he doesn't have one; he starts off going by "Tiger Eyes", becomes "Krake" when he joins Cobra, and then becomes Cobra Commander. What Happened to the Mouse?: Vanishes in theTime Skipbetween volumes 3 and 4; all we see of him is a poster on a wall. He's present among a gathering of heroes and villains convened to deal with Unicron.

characters.name: Doctor Mindbender
characters.description: Arbitrary Skepticism: Despite being fixated on the idea of the possibility of time travel,he scorns the idea of Destro's teleportation machine. The Bus Came Back: DuringRevolution, he's seen working withMiles Mayhem. But Not Too Foreign: His real name, "Armand Singh", suggest Sikh heritage, but he's not drawn darker than any of the other characters (and with hisimmaculately trimmed facial hair, he's unlikely to be a practicing Sikh). Embarrassing Nickname: Hereallyhates being called "Mindbender". Series Continuity Error: Dialogue and character pages inM.A.S.K.give him the name of "Verstal Bender", though the narration still uses "Armand Singh".Later given anAuthor's Saving Throwwhen his profile says that "Dr. Bender" is a cover he uses to avoid arrest.

characters.name: Tomax Paoli
characters.description: Chronic Backstabbing Disorder:HisGambit Speed Chessinvolves turning himself over to the Joes manipulating Clockspring into betraying them. Dragon Ascendant: In volume 4, he's become the leader of Cobra after theTime Skip. Gambit Speed Chess: Very good at adapting his plans on the fly. Happiness in Slavery: Believes in this thoroughly, and thinks it's why he and his brother are so happy; they have to answer to each other. (His brother disagrees.) Legacy Character: InRevolutionaries, Baron Ironblood tries to make him the next Cobra Commander. Tomax absolutely refuses, though.

characters.name: Xamot Paoli
characters.description: Happiness in Slavery: Initially believed in this, like his brother, untilhis fateful encounter with Chuckles. Killed Off for Real:When Chuckles detonates the nuclear bomb and destroys Section Twenty. Rage Within the Machine: He started as a member of Cobra, then soured on it. Slowly Slipping Into Evil: Well,Chaotic Evil. Though evil from the start, he steadily becomes more chaotic and unstable as time goes on.

characters.name: Crystal Ball
characters.description: Hypnotic Eyes: Has hypnotic powers. Mad Oracle: Claims to see the future, and the rest of Cobra aren't too sure about his sanity. Manipulative Bastard: Is content with manipulating Cobra from behind the scenes... until he finds out that the new Commander doesn't particularly care to listen to his advice. Vagueness Is Coming: In volume 5, he warns of "the horrors beneath the Earth".

characters.name: Copperback
characters.description: Rewarded as a Traitor Deserves: Turns Destro over to Cobra after he has her father killed to save both their lives. Violent Glaswegian: Scottish, and a lot more hot-tempered than Destro is.

characters.name: Croc Master
characters.description: Abusive Parents: His father didn't like him much. Non-Indicative Name:Averted, for once. Croc Master's father thought that "Croc Master" sounded better than "Gator Master", and kept a couple of crocodiles to justify it.

characters.name: Mad Monk
characters.description: Aborted Arc: His initial story had him placed under Krake by a Cobra psychologist to sabotage him, but when he reappears in volume 3, he's a loyal follower. Even Evil Has Loved Ones: The only thing he truly cares for is his wife and daughter...so Krake sends them to an internment camp to ensure his cooperation. Expansion Pack Past: Given one with Duke in volume 3. Wild Card: Due to hiscomplete lack of imaginationand incapability of self-deception, his actions can't be predicted.

characters.name: The Dreadnoks
characters.description: Awesome Aussie: Most of them, though Zandar and Zarana are British. Chainsaw Good: Buzzer. Dumb Muscle: Most of them, but especially Roadpig. Kill It with Fire: Torch and Burn Out. It's Personal: After their first meeting, Roadpig has it out for Roadblock.

characters.name: Big Boa
characters.description: Affably Evil: Genuinely considers Chuckles a friend, and is heartbroken afterhe assassinates Cobra Commander. Not in This for Your Revolution: He doesn't care about Cobra's ideology; he's "just here to box", and appreciates the kindness that Cobra Commander showed him. The Juggernaut: None of the other Cobra members can beat him in a fight.Chuckles only breaks his hands trying to fight him, and only wins by unexpectedly catching him in the throat with the slide of his pistol. Undying Loyalty: To Cobra Commander. Truer to the Text: A lot closer in design to the classic Big Boa, complete with the same helmet.

characters.name: Kallikhan
characters.description: It's Personal: With Snake Eyes. We Hardly Knew Ye: Existed just to be a Cobra Civil War candidate killed off by Snake Eyes.

characters.name: Vargas
characters.description: Hoist by His Own Petard: Gets infected by the bioengineered plague he had made to kill Duke with, and then ends upburstingwhen a cure is being tested on him. Man of Wealth and Taste: Is always impeccably dressed. (Not that it helps him in the end.) We Hardly Knew Ye: Pretty much just existed to be one of the Cobra Civil War candidates killed off by the Joes.

characters.name: Oda Satori
characters.description: Dead Person Impersonation:Gets killed and replaced by Zartan on Krake's orders.

characters.name: Soft Master
characters.description: Adaptational Villainy: The Marvel Comics Soft Master was a kindly and helpful mentor to Snake Eyes. Evil Mentor: To Snake Eyes. Good Scars, Evil Scars: Is heavily injured thanks to Snake Eyesthrowing the acid and neutralizing agent that he was meant to drink into the Soft Master's face. Guile Villain: What the "soft" in his name refers to. Humans Are Bastards: Believes in this.

characters.name: Chimera
characters.description: Expy: Larry Hama clearly based him off of the Marvel Comics version of Cobra Commander, most likely due to intending him to be this continuity's version of Cobra's leader. For the Evulz: As it turns out, his motivation is this: he just wants to cause as much destruction as possible. Never Found the Body: His body isn't recovered after his supposed death, something that waspresumablymeant to lead-in to him founding Cobra, butlater reveals make this impossible. Pater Familicide: Kills his family before (supposedly) killing himself. What Happened to the Mouse?: Chimera's story initially appeared to imply that he will become Cobra Commander (as made evident by the character's similarities to the Marvel Comics continuity's version of the character and appearing to fake his death after successfully setting up a pyramid scheme), but later installments of this continuity provide irreconcilable revelations of Cobra's origins, leaving the actual fate of Chimera and the repercussions of his scheme unaddressed.

characters.name: Hard Master
characters.description: Aw, Look! They Really Do Love Each Other: Despite hisGrumpy Old Manattitude, it becomes plain that he really does care about Snake Eyes and Alondra. Cynical Mentor: Doesn't approve of Snake Eyes giving out training to a schoolgirl. Defector from Decadence: Though it's never explained why he left the Arashikage. Intergenerational Friendship: With Alondra. Jerk with a Heart of Gold

characters.name: Alondra
characters.description: The Apprentice: To Snake Eyes, and later the Hard Master. Intergenerational Friendship: With the Hard Master. Little Miss Badass: Gives her bullies a beatdown after martial arts training from Snake Eyes. Parental Neglect: Says outright that her parents don't care where she is, and we only ever see her with the Hard Master afterwards. Wax On, Wax Off: Some of her training takes this form. That, orshe's just doing chores for him; it's not entirely clear.

characters.name: Scoop
characters.description: G.I. Joe's private reporter. Heart Is an Awesome Power: His media savviness does sometimes help in convincing government higher-ups that the Joes' mission achieved an overall positive result, even if it did not exactly fulfill the goal that was laid out beforehand. Heel–Face Turn: InOperation Dragonfire, Scoop starts out as an undercover Crimson Guardsman spying on G.I. Joe, who he blames for destroying his home. Of course, he eventually learns Cobra is the true culprit. New Meat: One issue of Special Missions had him tagging along on a covert op to record everything that goes down to satisfy a new DOD directive. His squadmates resent having to educate him every step of the way on the things that aren’t covered in basic training — e.g. if you have to drink from your canteen, finish the whole quart or else the enemy might hear water sloshing around as you move. Tuckerization: He is modeled and named after the NBC reporterMike Leonard.

characters.name: William Kessler-Latta
characters.description: The adult son of Cobra Commander, who was kept far away from his criminal activities, but eventually became a target for Cobra and G.I. Joe's intelligence unit. Action Survivor: He's an ordinary person who still finds himself getting involved with the G.I. Joe vs. Cobra conflict. Adaptation Name Change: From "Kessler" to "Kessler-Latta",afterChris Latta, Cobra Commander's voice actor fromthe animated series. Chronic Hero Syndrome: His location gets found out after he saves a group of tourists from drowning, getting his face onto the internet. Living MacGuffin:A pin in his leg contains a memory stick with huge amounts of data on Cobra's operations.

characters.name: Garrison "Blitz" Kreiger
characters.description: Adaptation Species Change:Due to turning out to be this continuity's version ofMerklynn, he is a Prysmosian here rather than a human being. Adaptational Villainy:He is revealed at the end ofFirst Striketo be aComposite Characterwith Merklynn fromVisionaries. While the original Merklynn was at worst morally ambiguous, this version of the character is straight up evil. The Bad Guy Wins:At the end ofFirst Strike, he manages to successfully drain Cybertron's energy and gets away without being caught. Composite Character:The end ofFirst Strikereveals that his true identity is Merklynn, the wizard who was theBig GoodofVisionaries. Corrupt Corporate Executive: Around the late 80s, he founded I.R.O.N., to gain more connections, and more access to Cybertronian tech.

characters.name: Bildocker
characters.description: Large and in Charge: Sort of. He's a bit pudgy, but he's not a leader. Leaning on the Fourth Wall: One issue of Special Missions (2013) has him showing off an action figure of himself to Roadblock, Mainframe, and Dial Tone, only to get mocked by the first two. The Friend Nobody Likes: Number 3. He's only on the Joe team because Hawk wanted him for hisrequisition skills.

characters.name: Clutch
characters.description: A mechanic and driver of the VAMP jeep. He gets a far bigger role in the comic than he ever did in the cartoon, and gets one of the biggest roles out of the original squad of "green fatigues" guys. Adaptational Intelligence: In Skybound'sEnergon Universehe has an engineering degree from MIT. Adaptation Name Change: During Devil's Due continuity, his code name was changed to "Double Clutch". Abhorrent Admirer: To Scarlett, Cover-Girl... well, any of his female teammates really. Badass Driver: Usually of the Vamp Mark II Jeep.

characters.name: Risk
characters.description: Accidental Misnaming: He and Duke get off on the wrong foot when Risk tries to tell the team that it won’t do “Heavy Duty” (he meant Rock’n’Roll) any good to mope about his death. Badass Boast: Gives a epic one in issue #24 while fighting off Crystal Ball's fear constructs.Risk:People think I took on the name "Risk" because I'm some kind of thrill seeker. My bosses though I had a death wish. But, no, I took that name...because I am the risk! Badass Bookworm: He's deadly in a straight fight, but his specialty is in analyzing risks and planning out how to eliminate them. Badass in a Nice Suit: Always seen in a fancy suit Canon Foreigner: The first wholly original character created for this series.

characters.name: Shooter
characters.description: GI Joe's first sniper who only later made an appearance. Action Girl: Comes with being a woman and GI Joe. Cold Sniper: Very good at taking out individuals from a distance with little emotion. The Ghost: They had their codename listed but not their face on the original Joe team list during the comic's early run. Killed Off for Real: In the Devil's Due comics that are now discontinuity.

characters.name: Snow Job
characters.description: Adaptational Angst Upgrade: In this series, Snow Job has been living with guilt for years over accidentally causing the death of his best friend Frostbite. The Aloner: When Frostbite died on a secret ski trip gone wrong, Snow Job blamed himself entirely and never got over it until the Joes cross his path. He's introduced living alone in an isolated snowy mountain range wasting his life away from society as a self-inflicted punishment. He nearly kicks the Joes off his land since he refuses to socialize, even with his other pal Tunnel Rat. Fortunately, the Joes help him get over his trauma. Bash Brothers: An arctic variant. Snow Job, Frostbite, and Tunnel Rat were all best friends while serving their country. Thick as thieves, loved getting into unofficial fun, rode rough slopes, and always had each others backs. It's why Frostbite's death hit him so hard. Beard of Sorrow: In this version, Snow Job's iconic beard is redesigned to give him an unkempt, depressing appearance. A major hint towards his downward spiral after his tragic past. Con Artist: Like his original counterpart, Snow Job has a way in roping people into his schemes, which is the reason why he has the call sign.

characters.name: Mercer
characters.description: Adaptational Villainy:Played With. Mercer is usually introduced as adefector from Cobrain other continuities. In this universe, we're introduced to him before he's had to a chance to perform hisHeel–Face Turnand he's currently serving as Destro's right hand man. Badass in Distress: He's captured by Risk in issue #24 and held prisoner by the Joes. It's implied this is what will start his defection from Cobra. Even Evil Has Standards: Clearly has some reservations about working with Cobra Commander, which he voices to Destro audibly. Number Two: Destro's sidekick, head of operations, and top soldier. Often seen at his boss's side. Sleeves Are for Wimps: Is often seen in sleevless uniforms. Even his combat outfit lacks them.

characters.name: Bludd
characters.description: Arc Villain: Of issues #8 through #11, as he antagonized Baroness and Cover Girl in a revenge scheme. Combat Pragmatist: Admits to using whatever means necessary to get the job done. Eye Scream: Gets shot by the Baroness across the head loses his left eye.His attempt at revenge on the Baroness with a knife fight ends with him losing the other one. Electronic Eyes:After losing both of his eyes in combat he's outfitted with cybernetic replacements. Hand Cannon: Carries a sizable revolver as his weapon of choice.

characters.name: Tomax & Xamot
characters.description: Big Bad Wannabe: The two of them really act like they're going to crush Destro in his series, but while they certainly do have some might to back themselves up, they aren't really on Destro's level, and time Destro comes closest to death, while appearing to be orchestrated by the twins, is actually done by Overkill a separate entity who's the real threat. In the end Destro beats them pretty thoroughly, though he lets them live thanks to the assets they can provide Cobra. Synchronization: Like in the cartoon, the two share a telepathic bond that allows them to feel whatever the other feels.

characters.name: Laszlo Vandermeer
characters.description: Death Seeker: He hates being forced to make Energon for Cobra so much that he regularly pleads with people to just put him out of his misery. The Commander isn’t likely to let that happen. Kidnapped Scientist: Just like his Sunbow counterpart, he's introduced as being a prisoner of Dreadnoks to make energon for them to sell. Once the Commander discovers him, the good doctor think he's here to rescue him and is horrified to find out he merely changed masters.

characters.name: Raptor
characters.description: Adaptational Badass: Raptor was something of aCreator's Pestto Larry Hama, who found him ridiculous, made a big joke of his filecard bio, and had Cobra Commander regard him with derision in-universe; there isn’t a trace of that here, marking the first time he’s portrayed as a serious threat. Attack Animal: He has his trained hawks to help him do his dirty work. Psycho for Hire: Forgiving the pun, he’s obviously cuckoo. Bludd hires him to attack Baroness and Cover Girl and later to kill Baroness's parents if something goes wrong.

characters.name: Medusa
characters.description: Ascended Extra: Starts as just another member of the Valkyries, but impresses the Commander enough that he eventually upgrades her. Canon Foreigner: She’s an original addition to COBRA’s roster, created for this comic. Co-Dragons: After her upgrade, the Commander declares her to be his left hand, equal to Destro being his right hand. Dark Mistress: Designed to be Cobra Commander's "girlfriend". Upon her introduction to Destro, the Commander says that she is "his". I Know What You Fear: Thanks to the D.I.R.E. tech, she's able to bring illusions of people's fears to life.

characters.name: Ripper
characters.description: Adaptational Sympathy: Ripper still isn't a good person by any means since he was still with the Dreadnoks. However, he's essentially press ganged into becoming the Commander's first minion, and after the Commander practically killed most of his clan, he knows he'll never be able to escape cleanly. Boisterous Bruiser: Brutal and loud, Ripper loves to trash talk as he throws down with enemies. Genre Savvy: When Cobra Commander appears to grant him his freedom, Ripper knowsdamnwellhe's just going to shoot him in the back the second Ripper turns around, so he chooses to stay. The Starscream: Swears loyalty to the Commander out of pragmatism, but most characters are aware he's just biding his time. He ends up single-handedly crippling Cobra Commander and taking out his entourage in the opening issue of the "Dreadnok War". Those Two Guys: Is this with fellow Dreadnok Buzzer. They get seperated briefly during the events ofCobra Commanderbut get reunited during the Dreadnok War arc of theG.I. Joebook.

characters.name: Buzzer
characters.description: Accidental Murder: It's heavily implied he accidently killed fellow Dreadnok Thrasher after a high five went wrong on account of Buzzer's new chainsaw hand. Chainsaw Good: As always, his primary weapon is a chainsaw. When he debuts in theGI Joecomic series he's replaced a hand with his chainsaw. Genius Bruiser: Subverted. He used to be a teacher before becoming obessed with biker gangs and joining the Dreadnok's, but he's doesn't seem to show any smarts and considering that he tried to high five Thrasher with his chainsaw hand, he can't be all that bright. Those Two Guys: With Ripper.

characters.name: Torch
characters.description: Cool Shades: As is the usual. In all likelihood they provide eye protection from the bright flames of his flamethrower. Demoted to Extra: Downplayed. Torch has never been the most important character, but in the cartoon he formed aTerrible Triowith Buzzer and Ripper. Here Buzzer and Ripper areThose Two Guysand often the one's most interacting with the Joes and Cobra Commander while Torch is very much aMauve Shirtfound with the rest of the Dreadnoks. The Stoic: Much quieter and reserved when compared to his loud comrades.

characters.name: Zander
characters.description: No True Scotsman: Zandar considers Buzzer to not be true Dreadnok blood, having been a teacher before joining the Dreaknok's. The Commander's uses this to manipulate Buzzer into fighting Zandar.

characters.name: Golobulus
characters.description: Adaptational Badass: In his original movie depiction, it was implied that he wasn’t much of a fighter, given how badly he lost in a one-on-one. Here, while still very much aOrcus on His Throne, appears much more equipped for combat, as shown when he takes onMegatronand stabs out of his remaining eye, forcing the Decepticon leader to flee for his life. Adaptational Wimp: His movie counterpart ran Cobra-La unopposed, but here he’s shown to be a complacent reactionary ruler who’s dealing with resource storages and rebellions. In the Hood: Introduced inCobra Commanderissue #1 in a red hood, though his ocular implant can be seen. Orcus on His Throne: His presence in the wider Energon Universe is mostly shown through his minions, such as the assassins he sends to kill Cobra Commander and the scouts led by Pythona to gather information on Cybertronians. Snake People: His lower half is serpentine.

characters.name: Nemesis Enforcer
characters.description: Adaptational Intelligence: In the Energon Universe, he's shown to be fully sapient; being able to speak, plan, and emote, unlike his animated counterpart. Canon Character All Along: He was disguised as a seemingly normal-looking man that went nameless before being revealed as Nemesis Enforcer in issue #3. Character Death:Was killed by Cobra Commander after trying to kill him. The Handler: Was tasked with protecting the Commander on his mission in the outside world.Except he's actually an assassin tasked with killing the Commander once he's served his purpose. Made of Iron: Through theCobra Commandermini-series, he gets shot repeatedly, bit by a giant python, takesa chainsaw to the face, and doesn't so much as budge. This is before he's revealed to be Nemesis by the way.

characters.name: Pythona
characters.description: Adaptational Nice Girl: She’s still a deadly enforcer of the shady Cobra-La nation set on wiping out the Transformers, but she's not all rough edges. InVoid Rivals, she permits Darak and Solillia to ride off the Sacred Ring with themafter the Quintessons take it overand later apologizes to Darak for lashing out at him when the Leviathan died. Broken Tears: She sobs as she cries over the death of theirLiving Ship, the Leviathan. Character Overlap: After they discover that Cobra Commander had lied to them about the extraterrestrials that have infiltrated Earth, Golobulous sends Pythona on a fact-finding mission in space, leading to her appearances inVoid Rivals. Dark Action Girl: Doesn’t get to do much in theCobra Commandermini-series, but she later gets time to show her skills of murder and violence inVoid Rivals, such as when she and her squad cuts up Skuxxoid into ribbons. Even Evil Has Loved Ones: She treasured theLiving ShipLeviathan, being an ancient symbol of hope for her people. When it dies escaping the Quintessons, she break out into tears as she sings its praises.

characters.name: Dr. Archibald Monev
characters.description: Comic-Book Movies Don't Use Codenames: Averted. He’s regularly called by his given name by other characters, however the press has dubbed him “Doctor Poison”, which he detest. Death by Adaptation: Killed by Cobra Commander after being forced to power the Brainwave Scanner.

characters.name: Matt Trakker
characters.description: For more information on him, seehere.

characters.name: Lt. Stone
characters.description: The Leader: He's the one who calls the shots. No Name Given: The toy bios of all the other Joes give out their full name, while Lt. Stone's name is only given as "Stone".

characters.name: Sgt. Savage
characters.description: Fish out of Temporal Water: He's a soldier from the 1940's now living in the show's current time. Human Popsicle: He was frozen until he thawed out in today's time. Number Two: To Stone; he takes charge in Stone's absence.

characters.name: Black Dragon
characters.description: Expy: While the Extreme line based their characters on various Joes, Black Dragon is just blatantly Snake Eyes. They're even both blonde! The only difference is, Black Dragon is NOTThe Speechless. Race Lift: In a pretty spectacular manner, all things considered. He only appeared in one franchise and this happened to him. His bio establishes him as being Chinese, yet he has constantly been depicted as a blond-haired guy.

characters.name: Freight
characters.description: The Big Guy: He visibly towers over the rest of the Joes. Especially impressive given theHeroic Buildof his comrades. Dynamic Entry: His first appearance sees him hurling himself out of a Jet ontoSKAR'sbase, using only blaster fire to cushion his landing.

characters.name: Metalhead
characters.description: Not to be confused with ARAH's Metal-Head. Hidden Depths: Looks and sounds like a stereotypical, well, metalhead. Heisone, but he's also a skilled technologist and soldier. Musical Assassin: Metalhead has a gun that plays rock music as a weapon. It blows up theMecha-Mookswith ease. The Power of Rock: He weaponizes rock music. The Mole: In the series finale, he pretends to turn traitor in order to help bring down SKAR.

characters.name: Quickstryke
characters.description: Heel–Face Turn: Was an agent of SKAR until his brother was killed by their experiments. My Nayme Is: His codename is spelled Quickstryke, rather than Quick Strike. Toyless Toyline Character: Like Mayday, there is no toy of him, but one was planned for an unreleased wave 2.

characters.name: Iron Klaw
characters.description: A ruthless masked terrorist in charge of the military wing of SKAR, he moonlights asCount von Raini, the leader of a small European nation. Skilled, manipulative and a master of disguise. Bad Boss: In the comic, he routinely kills his own troops, including for reasons as petty as someone accidentally touching him.Mean Boss: In the cartoon, he's not as actively malicious although he clearly cares little for the well-being of his troops. HisEstablishing Character Momentin the first episode is violently slapping down a SKAR soldier who accidentally called him Iron Klaw while he is still in his Count Von Rani guise. Mean Boss: In the cartoon, he's not as actively malicious although he clearly cares little for the well-being of his troops. HisEstablishing Character Momentin the first episode is violently slapping down a SKAR soldier who accidentally called him Iron Klaw while he is still in his Count Von Rani guise. Bastard Understudy: The Dark Horse comic reveals he assassinated his predecessor, the Duchess of Mklavia. Big Bad: He is the main antagonist, being the leader of SKAR and all.

characters.name: Inferno
characters.description: A pyromaniac with an irritating laugh and a bad sense of humor. Has a childlike mentality, regarding warfare as a game and the vehicles and weapons under his command as "toys". Ace Pilot: He's often seen piloting the Skystalker jet, and his Toy bios state his role in SKAR is "Jet Squadron leader", which is odd as there's nothing pilot-like about his design. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Is a recurring character in the first season of the cartoon but doesn't appear at all in the second, though a target dummy modeled after him does show up in "The Silencers" and he is mentioned by Rampage in "Wreckage: Revenge". Evil Has a Bad Sense of Humor: His first file card notes that he's a "notorious joker who's anything but funny".' "When is a runway no longer a runway? When it's BLOWN AWAY, ah-ha!''" Freudian Excuse: He was bullied by two rich kids when he was a child.

characters.name: Rampage
characters.description: An arms dealer who turns into a greenHulk-like monster when irritated, he supplies SKAR withMecha-Mooksand other weapons. He has sights on SKAR's leadership, but begrudgingly grovels under Iron Klaw's command until the right opportunity comes along. Berserk Button: Anything can aggravate Rampage if it escalates enough, but being bossed around will instantly set him off."NOBODY GIVES ME ORDERS!" Contrasting Sequel Antagonist: Rampage is in many ways similar to Destro fromG.I. Joe: A Real American Hero. Both are businessmen who supply robots and devices to the bad guys and are the most recurring villain next to the main antagonist, both wear some kind of armor withintegrated hand guns, and both are not afraid to voice their contempt for the main villain. However where Destro was cool and professional, Rampage is an unhinged, treacherous maniac. Depending on the Writer: Whether the gun on his shoulder works as a chaingun or a rocket launcher varies by episode. Large Ham: Yet another hammy villain. He especially hams it up when he's angry.

characters.name: Steel Raven
characters.description: The Dragon: She is Iron Klaw's second-in-command.

characters.name: Wreckage
characters.description: A soldier who formerly served with Freight. He was shot down during an unnamed war in South America and apparently into a grotesque cyborg by the Inter-Alliance. The Brute: A towering cyborg, he serves as Iron Klaw's field leader and attack dog. Cyborg: His right arm ends in a cybernetic hand that allows him to shoot lasers from his fingertips. Genius Bruiser: He's got both brawn and brains. Heel–Face Turn: In "Wreckage: Revenge", he finally learns that Iron Klaw is responsible for making him a cyborg and even contemplates joining the Joes at the end of the episode.

characters.name: GI Joe In General
characters.description: Badass Normal: As always, they're normal people who accomplish amazing feats. Beware the Nice Ones: G.I. Joe has some friendly and heroic people among the unit. All of whom are fully experienced elite soldiers capable of taking on mutant monsters and terrorists who outnumber them. "Dreadnoks Rising" serves as the best example when Zartan and his goons drastically mistake them as wannabe heroes who are no threat only to lose badly when they fight back. Chronic Hero Syndrome: Trouble never happens upon the Joes until the Joes confront trouble. Deadpan Snarker:All of them, butespecially Tunnel Rat. Like true soldiers, the Joes aren't above sarcastically ribbing each other over foolish or quirky moments. The Determinator: Despite being heavily outnumbered, outclassed, and alone, the team will do everything in their power to expose COBRA for the true evil monsters they are.

characters.name: Ripcord
characters.description: Voice Actor:Khary Payton Adaptational Badass:The first Ripcord to ever wield super powers. Black Guy Dies First:He appears to die in the series premiere. Subverted in "Prodigal", where it turns out that he survived. Came Back Wrong:Survived the explosion from the 1st episode but was infused with Bio-Viper material.Came Back Strong:Once he gets his chip removed, though, his Bio-Viper abilities become very useful to himself and the team. Came Back Strong:Once he gets his chip removed, though, his Bio-Viper abilities become very useful to himself and the team.

characters.name: US Military in General
characters.description: Inspector Javert: While Flint is the one that plays this the most straight, the entirety of the military pursuing the Joes falls under this as they are trying to capture the heroes all the while thinking they're the villains.

characters.name: Tripwire
characters.description: The explosive disposal expert of the G.I. Joe team. Comic Relief: Involuntarily if you will, but he's your to-go guy when doomsday clock is ticking.Find a panel in his first thirty appearances where heisn'ttripping over his own two feet. Only in IDW Publishing is he allowed to be a soldier outside of explosives. Find a panel in his first thirty appearances where heisn'ttripping over his own two feet. Only in IDW Publishing is he allowed to be a soldier outside of explosives. Crouching Moron, Hidden Badass: He is very clumsy most of the time, but when he's close to a bomb becomes an all-business professional. Death Seeker: His IDW incarnation deliberately takes dangerous risks; he doesn’t fear death because he sees it as reuniting with his girlfriend, who was killed in a London bus bombing.

characters.name: Cobra In General
characters.description: Adaptational Badass: This version of Cobra is a more subversive enemy than the out-and-out terrorist organization of the Sunbow cartoon. They've successfully convinced the public that they're a philanthropic company with aims to better society, but it's all a front for their shady dealings behind closed doors. The Joes are constantly on the run from Cobraandthe United States government, and it isn't until the finale that Cobra is finally revealed for what they are to the public, but the company is so large and wields enough influence that they could still give the world a fight, which Cobra Commander vows. Animal Motifs: If you can think of a way to subtly or not-so-subtly link something back to serpentine imagery, Cobra have done it.ShopSmart andSave, this universe's Wal-Mart (even called "S-Mart" for short), for example. MegaCorp: The company has a lot of influence over the general public. Teeth-Clenched Teamwork: Outside of the COBRA and MARS agents not getting along, there's often discontent around the higher ups. Destro hates Mindbender and the pair have tried sabotaging each other more than once. Storm Shadow once tried to kill Mindbender after the doctor nearly electrocuted him, Tomax and Xamot signed on only to find themselves enslaved to COBRA, and the Commander doesn't really endear himself to anyone when he has his employees eaten by a big snake. Villain with Good Publicity: Again, no one knows what they're really up to. Until the finale.

characters.name: Tomax and Xamot
characters.description: Voice actor:Stephen Stanton Adaptational Badass: TheTwin Telepathythey possess not only connects their minds, but can also influence the minds of others in order to make them slaves bowing before their command. Something they were never capable of in past incarnations. Adaptational Ugliness: The twins here are far more ratty and sketchy compared to their usual suave, muscle-bound businessmen guise. Adaptational Wimp: Although they have very powerful mental prowess, they lack the acrobatics and combat skills they usually have. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: A common trait of cult leaders. The twins pretend to be enlightened minds who can help lost souls, help themselves to their bank accounts that is.

characters.name: Bio-Vipers
characters.description: Genetically engineered super-soldiers created by Dr. Mindbender, they are the primary "special product" that COBRA is developing during the course of the series. It was discovering the first Bio-Viper lab that resulted in the Joes being branded as renegades. Blob Monster: Bio-Vipers are fundamentally amorphous masses of plant-based gelatinous matter. However, they normally assume a more humanoid form, because this makes them more useful. Combat Tentacles: They can sprout these to attack, but later versions typically don't bother. Cyborg: The short-lived Mecha-Vipers are Bio-Vipers integrated into a heavily-armoredcombat exo-suit. Healing Factor: Because they're synthetic masses of gelatinous matter, they can reassemble their bodies with ease. It's hard to inflict a lingering injury.

characters.name: MARS in General
characters.description: An arms dealing organization run by theMcCullenfamily, with James/Destro currently at its head. While COBRA acts under the radar, MARS already has a reputation as a group of warmongers and as such COBRA keeps their partnership a secret. Inter-Service Rivalry: In the appropriately titled episode, "The Enemy of My Enemy", it's clear that Destro and Mindbender have a rivalry over whose product is the best: Bender's organic monsters vs. Destro's machines. By episode's end, MARS is absorbed into the greater COBRA hierarchy, although Destro and Bender don't stop trying to sabotage one another. A Lighter Shade of Black: MARS deals in weapons and encourages global destabilization. In spite of that, it's a much better company to work for than COBRA as you won't be fed to a giant snake if you fail. Meaningful Name: Outside of MARS being an anagram, its name ties it into the god of war. Significant Anagram: MARS is an anagram of arms; MARS is an arms-dealing group.

characters.name: Scrap-Iron
characters.description: Voice Actor:Phil LaMarr Bait the Dog: He first appears as a kind preacher offering hot drinks and food to the homeless. This is all a cover so he can find veterans and abduct them for unethical science experiments. Laser-Guided Karma: Maimed with the technology from the company he works for by Roadblock who he'd been experimenting on. Mauve Shirt: The most recurring minion character in the show. While Bludd and Zartan are mercenaries in their own right, Scrap-Iron's often in the show to provide a helping hand to whatever Destro has planned. Number Two: He seems to be Destro's second in command and oversees MARS's various schemes. His second appearance had him dressed for combat and had the series continued he may have taken up the role asThe Dragonto Destro.

characters.name: Iron Grenadiers
characters.description: 2D Visuals, 3D Effects: The series is rife with this for the robots and vehicles, but this is the first example of people in the series rendered in CG. Elite Mooks: More skilled and powerful than the ordinary Bio-Viper, but the Bio-Viper mechs out-skill them. The Worf Effect: They debut beating up the new version of the Bio-Viper and their debut ends with an even newer version throwing them around.

characters.name: Law & Order
characters.description: Canine Companion: Order is Law's best friend and will bite any criminal to submission. Big Damn Heroes: Law and Order rally a group of non-dirty guards to cut off the Warden's escape route, trapping him in his own mess. Dirty Coward: At first. He quietly keeps his disagreements of his corrupt prison to himself because he fears how one man can't stop a whole system of evil alone. Duke inspires him to restore faith in law and order. Everyone Has Standards: Is thoroughly disgusted by the prison's abuse towards convicts, especially ones like Duke who've committed rather minor felonies being starved to death. Evil-Detecting Dog: Order only snarls at dirty cops.

characters.name: Barbecue
characters.description: Arch-Enemy: To Firefly, as one loves causing fires while he fights them.His backstory very strongly implies that a teen Firefly caused fires in his town before with just a book of matches, which left him with severe burns and pushed him into becoming a firefighter. The Atoner: After successfully winning the battle against Firefly, Barbecue decides to stick around his home town to make up for his mistake in trusting COBRA by actually giving aid in rebuilding the city himself. Broken Pedestal: Cobra Industries was once a great company in his eyes as he truly thought their technological and economic advancement would save his dying mountain town. However, upon discovering that their dam was never real and the city receivednoneof the benefits promised to them, he's utterly shocked to see them for the snakes they really are. Crouching Moron, Hidden Badass: He spends half his debut being a blindly loyal Cobra defender, but it turns out he's a fully capable firefighter not afraid to rush into the literal heat of battle. Defector from Decadence: While initially loyal to Cobra Industries, he finally quits after seeing how evil they truly are.

characters.name: Timber
characters.description: Action Pet: He's Snake Eyes' wolf companion. As well as a loyal attack dog. Because You Were Nice to Me: How does he become friends with Snake Eyes? The ninja finds him in pain and caught in a trap, where he sets him free and heals his injury. From this point on, Timber sides with Snake as his best pal. Fire-Forged Friends: He becomes loyally devout to Snake Eyes when the ninja rescues him from a trap. The pair work together as a lethal partnership in combat for the rest of his debut story. Loyal Animal Companion: He befriends Snake Eyes after he rescued him from a trap. Timber then stays with Snow Job when the Joes leave. Noble Wolf: A loyal animal to his human compatriots.

characters.name: Red Star
characters.description: Arch-Enemy: To Baroness as she and her family tyrannically ruled over Red Star's people. Crazy-Prepared: As the rebel leader of an underground resistance, he has a plan if his old plans fail. Enemy Mine: He and the Joes are forced to ally when both their plans go up in smoke. Things are very rocky, but both sides grow an understanding of the other eventually. He Who Fights Monsters: His quest to take down the Baroness has resulted in him being just as coldhearted and ruthless as her. Duke has to convince him to care about the dozens of civilian casualties who are going to be caught in his crossfire, to which he is alright with at first. Heel–Face Turn: By the end of his team-up with the Joes he reconsiders his violent war tactics and becomes a more noble rebel over theKnight Templarhe used to be.

characters.name: Airtight
characters.description: Containment Clothing: He has to wear an airtight suit to prevent spreading the Anacaonda Strain to others. Distressed Dude: The majority of his debut is the Joes rescuing him. Et Tu, Brute?: He's entirely shocked that his lab partner for years, Dr. Monev, would turn on him by using him as a living test subject for their virus. Once Monev reveals the true venomous snake that he is, Airtight's hurt soon turns into sheer hatred. Handicapped Badass: An odd variant, but he fits. By the end of his origin tale, he's forced to wear an airtight enviro-suit designed to prevent him from spreading a lethal virus, but it keeps him alive and well enough to combat COBRA. Heroic Sacrifice: Tries to dive out of an airplane to save his daughter and the other passengers from the virus. Snake Eyes saves him.

characters.name: Sigma  6
characters.description: A Father to His Men: Like most incarnations of the character, he is something of a father figure to the other Joes. All-American Face: He's a good guy who fights for America. Indy Ploy: Duke is quite fond of these when he's out in the field, usually in some kind of deep trouble. Jack of All Stats: And because of this, he is able to fit in no matter what the team configuration for the current mission is. The Rival: To Cobra Commander.

characters.name: COBRA
characters.description: Actually a Doombot: When defeated by Duke at the end of theFive-Episode Pilotit turned out to be a robot duplicate he left behind as Cobra Commander set the giant submarine base to self destruct after itsWave-Motion Gunfired. Adaptational Badass: Perhaps the deadliest interpretation of Cobra Commander to date. This version is perfectly willing and able to engage in direct combat with his enemies, to the point where it seems only Duke is capable of fighting him on even terms. Bad Boss: HisEvil Planin theFive-Episode Pilotinvolved firing off aWave-Motion Gunfrom a giant submarine, and set the sub to self destruct after the cannon fired. As far the audiences knows, he did not let his subordinates in on this and planned to let them die. And when Sigma 6 manages to secure one of the Power Stones, he decides to take more drastic measures and sends out his subjects across the globe while threatening their lives should they fail to bring him even one stone. Cobra Commander even spells it out to Destro in an episode- if Destro succeeds in his mission, it's Cobra Commander's victory. If Destro fails, it's 'his' fault. Big Bad: Of Cobra andG.I. Joe: Sigma 6as a whole. Brought Down to Badass: His weapons once conventionally stopped working a fight with Duke, but he still managed to fight him on equal terms, though he ultimately lost.

characters.name: Other
characters.description: Four-Star Badass: He's a general. Reasonable Authority Figure: To the Sigma 6 Joes, even though he's not seen in an authoritative position much at all. Out of Focus: In this case though, the argument could be made that he wasn't really intended to be focused on much. Due to the events of"Valor Vs. Venom", he is recuperating in the hospital during the series proper. His biggest contribution is that of his son, Scott. Put on a Bus: Though he's mentioned, he doesn't show up at all in season 2. Toyless Toyline Character: He has no toy.

characters.name: Gen. Hawk
characters.description: Big Good: Of the first film, where he's the one in charge of the G.I. Joe task force. Reasonable Authority Figure: He picks operatives well and insists on getting good intelligence. Screw the Rules, I'm Doing What's Right!: Keeps the Joes on-mission even when he's been ordered to disband them- because a Joe has been captured and the world is in imminent danger. What Happened to the Mouse?: He doesn't appear in the second movie. All There in the Manual: The President of the United States(really Zartan)fires him from his position in Operation Hiss #5.

characters.name: Sgt. Stone
characters.description: G.I. Joe's special operations instructor who teaches combat training. The Cameo: He's only there for the training scene. Drill Sergeant Nasty: Downplayed. Expy:Sgt. Stone seems to be a replacement for the character/professional wrestler Sgt. Slaughter. Oddly, he's not the first Expy of him, with Beachhead having also filled the role. He also aligns with multiple "Lt. Stone" characters in Joe cartoons and comics.Some fans during their first viewings have gotten him mixed up with Flint, probably because he looks and acts even more like traditional depictions of Flint than the official movie Flint (played byD. J. Cotrona) that appeared in the sequel. Not only does he consistently sport a beret but has a similarly deep extroverted voice and commanding presence. Sgt. Stone seems to be a replacement for the character/professional wrestler Sgt. Slaughter. Oddly, he's not the first Expy of him, with Beachhead having also filled the role. He also aligns with multiple "Lt. Stone" characters in Joe cartoons and comics.

characters.name: Gen. Joe Colton
characters.description: The original G.I. Joe, who helps out Roadblock, Lady Jaye, and Flint. Adaptation Personality Change: Much more gruff than the easygoing Joe Colton from the comics. Big Good: He founded the Joes. Also, hejoins Roadblock's team and provides them with essential weapons and allies. Crazy-Prepared: He's got alotof weapons hidden in his kitchen, including a pair of grenades hidden in a bowl of fruit. Intergenerational Friendship: Develops one with Lady Jaye.

characters.name: Mouse
characters.description: Friendly Sniper: A sniper who cracks some jokes. We Hardly Knew Ye:Killed off in the purge.

characters.name: JamesMcCullen/ Destro
characters.description: A weapons designer and founder of the Military Armament Research Syndicate (MARS). His terrorist agenda sets up the movie's plot. Adaptational Villainy:Destro in the comics, while still technically a villain, is a much more honorable and principled man, and vestiges of this made it into the cartoon. Here, Destro has little in the way of redeeming values. Though he seems to believe the world is chaotic and that he's the only one who can fix it with himself asThe Man Behind the Man.Destro and the Baroness aregenuinely in love in both the comics and cartoon; here, the Baroness is mind-controlled into being with him, making the relationship of questionable consent at best and Destro into a much more despicable character.Though Destro did try to save her when the Doctor threatened to kill her to spite Duke, while also attempting to shoot Duke for saying that he didn't deserve her.
